summary: This stylesheet defines styles for a search input component with labels, helper text, and a results list. It uses CSS variables for theming and includes special accessibility handling for screen-reader-only text, focus states with smooth transitions, and a styled empty state with an image.

explanations.7: The `composes` keyword is a CSS Modules feature that lets this class inherit all styles from the `mk-eyebrow` class defined globally, then add its own styles on top.
explanations.12: This class hides content visually but keeps it accessible to screen readers by shrinking it to 1 pixel, hiding overflow, and using `clip-path` to ensure it's completely invisible.
explanations.19: The `clip-path: inset(50%)` crops away 50% from all sides, ensuring the already-tiny element is truly hidden rather than just off-screen where it might be found.
explanations.27: The `font-family: inherit` makes the input use whatever font its parent container uses, instead of falling back to the browser's default form font.
explanations.33: The `transition` property creates smooth animations for two properties—the border color and shadow—over 0.15 seconds when the input gains focus.
explanations.38: The `::placeholder` pseudo-element targets the placeholder text (the hint text shown before you type), letting you style it separately from the actual input text.
explanations.42: The `:focus` pseudo-class targets the input when it's actively selected, removing the browser's default outline and replacing it with custom border and shadow styling.
explanations.56: The `list-style: none` removes the default bullet points from a list, and the flex layout with `column` direction stacks the items vertically.
explanations.96: The `flex: 0 0 auto` tells the flexbox not to shrink or grow this image, keeping it at exactly 56x56 pixels even if there's space pressure.
